title: What is AIoT and why use it?

spans.text: IoT devices connect to a network and send data. AIoT (Artificial Intelligence of Things) adds machine-learning decisions: a device can interpret sensor readings instead of only forwarding them. For example, a microphone can recognize a simple clap locally, or a vibration sensor can flag a pattern that may indicate a machine problem.

Why use it? Local decisions are faster, can work without internet, and may avoid sending raw audio or personal data to the cloud. Cloud inference uses a powerful remote computer and keeps the device simple; edge AI runs the model on the device or a nearby gateway. A small ESP32 needs a small model and a narrowly defined task.

Examples include estimating room occupancy, spotting unusual vibration, recognizing a sound event, or detecting signs of a dry plant. A model output is a prediction, not a guarantee. Keep ordinary limits and a safe fallback for important controls.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Do not let AIoT control a safety-critical function by itself. Models can be wrong; define confidence limits, ordinary sensor checks, and a fallback first.
